[USER] User expressed interest in the process for deciding which book wins the Man Booker Prize.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The process for deciding the Man Booker Prize winner includes submission, longlisting, shortlisting, and winner selection.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Publishers must submit their entries by the deadline.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Judges create a longlist of up to 13 titles in September.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Judges narrow down the longlist to a shortlist of six books in October.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Judges read the shortlisted books again and hold discussions to decide on the winner, announced at a ceremony in October or November.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Judges are appointed by the Man Booker Foundation and change every year, typically consisting of writers, critics, and literary figures.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Judges base their decision on literary merit, originality, accessibility, author's skill in using English, and the book's contribution to the genre.  
[USER] User found the process comprehensive.  
[USER] User inquired if judges ever choose more than one winner.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Typically, the Man Booker Prize judges choose only one winner, but there have been occasions of joint winners.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The prize was shared in 1974 between Nadine Gordimer for "The Conservationist" and Stanley Middleton for "Holiday".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The prize was shared again in 1992 between Michael Ondaatje for "The English Patient" and Barry Unsworth for "Sacred Hunger".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Since then, the prize has always been awarded to a single winner.  
[USER] User expressed surprise at the joint winners in the past.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Man Booker Prize has a rich history of recognizing outstanding works of fiction in the English language.  
[USER] User agreed that the Man Booker Prize highlights some of the best works of fiction.
